newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening lower on profit-taking.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 20289.93 -242.62 LME CASH NICKEL US$7210 +25.0
CANDLR 1.3855 LME CASH ALUM US$1602.5 +17.5
CAN 30-YR 114.60 +0.12 BRENT CRUDE US$17.64 +0.14

--------------------MARKET COMMENT---------------------------- * Toronto stocks were expected to soften at the open in the absence of key economic news. * Traders said market cannot sustain rise much longer and profit-taking likely to set in.
Toronto stocks were expected to open softer on Wednesday as profit-taking sets in to the market, which has hovered near all-time highs recently.

"I think we'll go lower. There isn't a whole lot of economic news coming out today....I just think it's time for some profit-taking. I mean you can't have 400 points on little or no real news," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index gained 5.63 points to close at 6473.04 on Tuesday.
The index lagged its New York counterpart, which added more than 60 points yesterday on solid blue chip performances.

"Maybe we're being more realistic in Canada than they are in the U.S. The big problem in the U.S. is there's so much money flow. When you get the U.S. government paying down the debt by the billions of dollars.... that money has to go somewhere," he said.
U.S. treasuries opened higher on Wednesday on short-covering ahead of anticipated friendly economic data later this week.
The trader said leaked news that Prime Minister Jean Chretien has reappointed deficit-slashing Paul Martin as finance minister will be well received, especially by Canadian dollar investors.
"I think that's positive. There's no question that he has been the leader, if you want, on fiscal reform," he said.

In economic news, Canada's new housing price index rose 0.8 percent in April to 132.7 (base 1986) from April 1996, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday. A Reuter survey of economists had forecast a 0.2 percent rise in the annual index.
